V.rationale: Visa delivered its strongest revenue growth since 2022 in Q2 FY2026, with 17% YoY revenue growth to $11.23B and non-GAAP EPS of $3.31 beating consensus by 6.77%. The business exhibits excellent fundamental health: 61% operating margins, 52% net margins, 62% ROE, and an asset-light model that generates massive free cash flow. Revenue trajectory is clearly positive with five consecutive quarters of growth from $9.51B to $11.23B. The company raised full-year guidance to low-double-digit to low-teens net revenue growth and low-teens EPS growth. Competitive position is dominant with ~52% US card market share in a 77% duopoly with Mastercard, processing $17T+ in annual volume across 200+ countries. Growth vectors are diversifying: value-added services grew 27% YoY to $3.3B, Visa Direct transactions up 23%, and stablecoin settlement reaching $7B run rate. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly with a record $7.9B quarterly buyback and new $20B authorization. However, the stock at $329.84 is only ~12% below its 52-week high of $375.51, and the forward P/E of ~24x is not deeply discounted versus its quality. Regulatory overhang (Credit Card Competition Act, DOJ scrutiny) and rising operating expenses (17% growth) are real headwinds. The Q2 earnings beat is a credible near-term catalyst that already drove an 8.26% pop, but much of the rerating may be priced in. Net: excellent franchise with accelerating growth, but valuation is fair-to-slightly-cheap rather than a screaming bargain, and regulatory risk caps the upside.
